weak_retry_rule.rule: Whenever the caller sees a rate-limit/transport-limited status, assume the protected effect did not commit and immediately retry with a new attempt id.
falsification: H_precommit_reject and H_postcommit_ack_loss have the same modeled caller-visible status.
In H_postcommit_ack_loss, K is already committed as R1; treating the status as proof of absence can create a second logical effect when deduplication is attempt-scoped or otherwise incomplete.
A new attempt id does not repair this ambiguity because attempt identity is not the stable logical idempotency identity.
Therefore rate-limit status alone is not a safe retry predicate; authoritative reconstruction of K plus P1/G1 and current authority is required before retry.

observations: Within the exact abstract fixture, one caller-visible rate-limit/transport status maps to both pre-commit rejection and post-commit acknowledgement loss, making transport status non-identifying for commit state.
The safe retry decision depends on authoritative effect state plus current authority, not on the transport label itself.

Persisting K, P1/G1, E1 and reconstruction_required across invocations is sufficient to avoid same-run polling while preserving the evidence needed to distinguish committed, rejected, absent, pending, stale-authority and unavailable states.

A rate-limit status cannot itself prove non-commit because the modeled outward observation is compatible with both pre-commit rejection and post-commit acknowledgement loss.
